texts.preamble: Da vs Mudassar Ansari on 27 May, 2024 In The Court Of Sh. Abhishek Kumar Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate-01 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi District: New Delhi Cr Cases 1387/2024 Delhi Administration Vs. Mudassar Ansari. Judgment
texts.facts: The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Cr. Case 1387-2024 Delhi Administration Vs.. Mudassar Ansari Page No. 1 of 8 PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of Section 2 (ia) (a) & (m) of the PFA Act. 2. Initially, after conclusion of the trial, the accused was convicted by the then, Ld. ACMM vide order dated 29.04.2017 under section 16(1)(a) of the PFA act read with section 7 of the PFA act and was accordingly sentenced. 3. The accused had challenged the order before the appellate court. On 15.02.2023, the following questio was framed by me: Accordingly, despite opportunity, the prosecution did not lead any evidence as well as the accused. During the course of arguments, the accused did not dispute the proceedings conducted by the department regarding the lifting of the sample or the subsequent proceedings. It is the case of the department that on 21.07.2010, the Food Official consisting of Food Inspector Gian Chand and Field Assistant Satish Gaur under the supervision of SDM/LHA Vivek Kumar Tripathi along with staff reached at the premises of M/s Lazeem Sweets Shop No. 8, Sector-5, R K Puram, New Delhi and found the vendor conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored/exposed for sale of human consumption. Thereafter, 750 grams of 'Paneer' was purchased as a sample from the vendor, which was lying in open tray bearing No Label or declaration and then as per the rules, was divided into three parts. 9. Further, the one sample was sent to the public analyst intact condition and other two counter parts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Thereafter, the Food Analyst vide its report dated 18.08.2010, found that the sample was not confirming to the standards prescribed on the ground that the percentage of the milk fat was less then the prescribed minimum limit of 50%. Then, upon the receipt of the report, investigation was directed which was carried out by the FI and after Cr. Case 1387-2024 Delhi Administration Vs.. Mudassar Ansari Page No. 4 of 8 obtaining sanction u/s 20 of the PFA Act, the complaint was filed in the court. 10. Further, the accused was summoned after taking cognizance and he preferred an application under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act and the second counter part of the sample was selected by the accused, which was sent to the Central Food Laboratory and the Director analyzed the sample and gave a report vide Certificate dated 14.12.2010, opining that the sample does not confirm to the standards. 11. Accordingly, notice was framed against the accused for the offence punishable u/s 7/16 (1) (a) of the PFA Act for the violation of section 2 (ia) (a) & (m). 12.
texts.arguments: The counsel for the accused has centered his arguments primarily on the ground that the sample in question which was examined by the CFL was not representative in character. He has emphatically argued that the sample in question was Paneer and it is a perishable item and subject to decay. He has relied upon several judgments in support of his contentions as well as the Journal, which was examined in the testimony of DW-1 and CW-1, to show that even if the Paneer is well preserved with addition of 0.4% formalin, the sample stored for a period of 7, 14 and 21 days will witness decrease in the fat present in the Paneer and if the Paneer is analysised after 21 days, the decrease will be at an average of 7.1% and thus, the fat percentage found by the CFL to be around 46% was the result of deterioration of the sample and it amply shows that the fat percentage at the time of lifting of the sample would have been more than 50% ie the minimum standard. Secondly, the prosecution has failed to show the method of analysis were the same as notified by the department. 6. On the other hand, Ld. SPP contended that the report of CFL is conclusive in nature and replaces the report of the PA and has categorically shown that the fat percentage was less then the minimum standard and it cannot be brush aside merely on the basis of research paper, which is Ex.DW1/A and all the parameters as per the Cr. Case 1387-2024 Delhi Administration Vs.. Mudassar Ansari Page No. 3 of 8 Regulations have been followed to prepare the report and no contradictions could be brought on record qua the same.
